rounds.proof_sketch: Mutation is in 'if (return_indices)' block. Model default is return_indices=False. When return_indices=False, function returns 'output' directly and the torch::cat line (containing the mutation) is never executed. 112 rounds of bitwise-identical results confirm this path is never taken.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation removes .unsqueeze(-1) from indices in the torch::cat operation, but this entire block is only executed when return_indices=True. The model's __init__ has return_indices=False as default, and the fixed configuration uses this default. Since return_indices=False, the function returns 'output' directly without executing the mutated torch::cat line. This explains why all 112 bitwise comparison rounds and 45 enhanced tests showed identical results - the mutation is in dead code for this configuration.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under the fixed-value contract. Killing this mutant requires setting return_indices=True in the model constructor, which is a configuration change prohibited by the contract. No value-level change to the input tensor [16, 64, 128] can trigger execution of the return_indices code path.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing frameworks should ensure test configurations cover all boolean flags and conditional code paths. For this kernel, separate test configurations with return_indices=True and return_indices=False should be maintained to achieve full path coverage of the CUDA code.
